title: You wake up 300 years late on a broken ship
dek: The briefing is missing, the crew is thin and the ship has a job for you. Twelve questions about what you would actually do.

questions.prompt: You wake from cryo 300 years late. The ship is intact. The crew is not.

options.label: Find the engine room. It's making a sound
Check the log for what happened
Look for a garden that still grows
Get a message to whoever sent us

questions.prompt: The ship's computer has taken a vote and has a job for you.

options.label: Give me the manual
Ask the computer why
Take the job, leave the paperwork
Ask what happens if I refuse

questions.prompt: The colony can bring one thing back from Earth:

options.label: A forest, seed by seed
Every book and every recording

questions.prompt: Kindness is a weakness in a survival situation.
I reread the same page because I forgot where I was.
The airlock opens and a stranger in an identical uniform claims they're you.

options.label: Check the serial number
Ask a question only you'd know
Offer them the couch
Close the airlock. Politely

questions.prompt: A message to the future is more useful than a message about the past.
There's a planet you could live on. One catch:

options.label: The ground is only semi-solid
The locals speak only in sound
The days last six months
The last colony left a working city, no explanations

questions.prompt: The ship is in a time loop. You've been through it six times.

options.label: Find the exit, take notes
Leave a message for next time
Use the time to learn something
Relax. Nothing you do matters

questions.prompt: I'd take the long trip alone if it meant seeing something new.
The best version of the future is quieter.
Earth stops replying. No distress signal, no news.

options.label: Keep sending. Every day
Work out what to do without them
Build something that lasts here
Sit down and think about what home was

results.name: The Ship's Mechanic
results.blurb: You hear the problem before anyone else does. While the bridge debates policy, you're already in the crawlspace with a torch and a theory. You don't need credit, but you would like the ship to stop making that noise.
strengths: Calm with a spanner in their hand
results.watchOut: You can't fix people with a spanner. Say the difficult thing out loud.

results.name: The First Contact Linguist
results.blurb: Before the weapons or the treaties, you want to know what they call themselves. You assume every misunderstanding is a translation problem and you are usually right. You'd rather ask a stupid question than make a permanent assumption.
strengths: Patient with people who are afraid
results.watchOut: Not everything is a misunderstanding. Sometimes the answer is no.

results.name: The Terraform Optimist
results.blurb: The planet is hostile, the timeline is centuries and you've started a garden. You think in generations rather than quarters, which makes you either visionary or unbearable at meetings. The seed you planted will matter to someone you'll never meet.
strengths: Turns a dead place into a project
results.watchOut: The people here now still need dinner. Don't only plan for the century.

results.name: The Ethics Officer
results.blurb: Every plan gets one question from you and everyone groans, because it's always the right question. You're not against progress — you just want to know who cleans up and who doesn't get a vote. Your existence makes the mission slower and better.
strengths: Sees the person outside the plan
results.watchOut: The perfect question can stall the airlock. Decide, then keep the concern.

results.name: The Colonist
results.blurb: You're not here for the science or the glory. You're here to make a place livable, with a door that shuts and a chair that's yours. You unpack before the briefing finishes and you are the reason the corridor smells like soup.
results.watchOut: Building a home can become hiding in it. Invite the crew in.

results.name: The Loop Auditor
results.blurb: You noticed the pattern on the second repeat and started taking notes on the third. While everyone else panics, you're testing variables and keeping a log. It's lonely being the only one who remembers — but someone has to keep the receipts.
strengths: Keeps the record nobody else does
results.watchOut: Noticing the loop doesn't get you out of it. Tell someone what you've seen.

results.name: The Reluctant Captain
results.blurb: You didn't ask for the bridge, but everyone was looking at you and the alarm was going. You make the call, take the blame and privately resent how much you enjoy it. Competence is a trap you walked into with your eyes open.
strengths: Protects the crew from the worst news
results.watchOut: You don't have to hold all of it. Tell one person the real situation.

results.name: The One Who Stays
results.blurb: While the others go to the surface or the stars, you stay with the ship, the records and the people who can't leave. Nobody makes a documentary about the one who stays. The whole thing falls apart without you in about four days.
results.watchOut: Staying is a choice, not an identity. Take the trip you keep declining.
